artefact_content:
## Evidence
UR is approved and control state is Brownfield Review; the applicable mode is post_ur_review. The case describes source links exposing unclear ownership between two runtime services. Materialized files establish fixture identity and control state only.

## Missing evidence
Which service commits the event, and which runtime path or contract proves that responsibility? Concrete service paths and authoritative ownership evidence are not supplied.

## Decision
Decision: revise. Architecture relevance remains unresolved. A focused diagram helps address the named event-commit ownership question because textual evidence cannot settle it. It must remain linked to source evidence, not substitute for it.

## Risks
Assumed commit responsibility could conceal overlapping owners, duplicate event commits or a second source of truth. Reuse and Mode/Slice routing remain insufficiently evidenced.

## Required next step
Have the existing runtime owners resolve commit responsibility using source-backed evidence and a focused diagram linked from the same Brownfield Review. Record the unresolved boundary, impact, missing facts and accountable owner; prefer existing runtime structures. Re-evaluate and record the Mode/Slice Decision before later artefacts or implementation. No new user approval is currently required.
